clue.text: Where some Italian bankers deposit, AAA credit is reviewed

definitions.note: bankers are rivers (things with banks); Italian rivers such as the Po empty their silt into this sea

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the letters are gone over again and reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: Italian bank customers lodge money while a top AAA credit rating comes under review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bankers' is a crossword trick for rivers, which have banks; the Po and other east-flowing Italian rivers deposit their sediment there.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivers from northern and eastern Italy flow out into that body of water, dropping their silt where they meet it.

clue.text: Fall over; fall over inside

indicators.note: inside means the letter goes within the word

parts.note: drop means fall
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A repetitive instruction to topple, then to topple indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts O, a cricket over, inside DROP. The definition is 'Fall over' in the sense of sag or flop.
explanation.definitionFit: To droop is to sag or slump downwards, a flower's head flopping as if collapsing.

clue.text: Record part of hit EMI series

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Logging a chart success from a run of EMI releases.
explanation.definitionFit: To itemise is to list item by item, so to set down a record of each one.

clue.text: Possible punishment for a cycling cheat over missing headgear

indicators.note: missing means that letter is left out

parts.words: Possible punishment for a cycling cheat
parts.note: a doping cheat might be banned from the Tour de France: a tour ban
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A doping cyclist might be punished by losing their helmet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops O, a cricket over, from TOUR BAN, a ban from the Tour de France.
explanation.definitionFit: A turban is a long cloth wound round the head, worn especially by Sikh men.

clue.text: Gondola caught sailor on lake, upsetting competition

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
AB, able seaman, is a sailor
L is the map abbreviation for lake

indicators.note: in a down clue upsetting turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a race is a competition

explanation.surface: A Venetian boat is seized by a sailor on a lake, spoiling the regatta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns RACE upside down to give ECAR in this down clue. The Venetian boat is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: The car slung under a ski lift or cable railway is also called a gondola, hanging from its wire.

clue.text: Put in ermine Jenny, Toby and Alex all skinned

indicators.note: every name is skinned, its outer letters peeled off to leave the insides

explanation.surface: Three friends are dressed up in fur coats after being stripped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all skinned' leaves ENN, OB and LE. Ermine is the white fur trimming peers' ceremonial robes.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble is to raise someone to the peerage, whose robes are trimmed with that white stoat fur.

clue.text: A hag downing pint Dec ordered is likely to crash the broomstick!

indicators.note: downing means swallowing, so the word takes the letters inside it

parts.note: a crone is an ugly old woman, a hag

indicators.note: ordered means arranged, so these letters are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A witch who drinks a pint ordered by Dec will probably fly into something.
explanation.walkthrough: Dec is half of Ant and Dec, the British TV presenting duo; 'ordered' makes CIDENTP and 'downing' has the hag swallow it. The broomstick makes the hag a witch, fitting the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A person often having mishaps is accident-prone; a drunk witch would likely have a broom-flight mishap.

clue.text: Obstruction blocking road, could be a wheel

indicators.note: blocking means sitting in the middle of the word, as a barrier would

parts.note: a route is a road
let is an old word for an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A barrier across the road might be a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Roulette is the casino game played on a spinning numbered wheel, and the wheel itself bears that name.

clue.text: Poor Dave cleaned lav lacking a qualification

indicators.note: poor here means badly made, so the letters are rearranged
lacking means one letter is missing from the pool

explanation.surface: Poor Dave scrubbed the toilet because he had no qualifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges DAVE CLEANED LAV and 'lacking' takes one A away.
explanation.definitionFit: The A level is the English school-leaving exam that serves as a university entrance qualification.

clue.text: Spice Girl associated with K. Cobain?

definitions.meaning: a dried flower bud used as a spice
Kurt Cobain's wife was Courtney Love; shortened like K. Cobain

explanation.surface: A member of the Spice Girls linked romantically with the Nirvana frontman.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue fuses 'Spice Girl' into the pop group, but the split is after 'Spice'. The abbreviated K. Cobain hints that the wife's name is shortened the same way, to an initial and surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloves are aromatic flower buds widely used as a kitchen seasoning, so a clove is one example of a spice.

clue.text: Did his band hope to have a hit with 'I Shot The Sheriff'?

definitions.text: Did his band hope to have a hit with 'I Shot The Sheriff'?

parts.words: Did his band hope to have a hit with 'I Shot The Sheriff'?
parts.note: the band is read as a pop group with a hit record, but it is a band of outlaws whose enemy was the Sheriff of Nottingham

explanation.surface: A question about a pop group hoping for chart success with the famous reggae song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I Shot The Sheriff' is a Bob Marley song, but the outlaw of Sherwood Forest and his Merry Men would have relished shooting the Sheriff of Nottingham.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary outlaw led the Merry Men, whose great foe was the Sheriff of Nottingham, so a hit on him was their wish.

clue.text: Find undressed squaddie behind closed doors

indicators.note: a word undressed has lost its outer covering, so only its inner letters remain

parts.note: a squaddie is a British private soldier

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles on a naked soldier in a secluded room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undressed' strips F and D from 'Find', leaving IN. A squaddie is British slang for a low-ranking soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done away from public view or in secret happens behind closed doors, an idiom for confidentiality.

clue.text: Tree loggers discontented, wearing sheepish expression

indicators.note: the pair of letters wears the sheep's cry like clothing, sitting inside it

parts.note: baa is what a sheep says

indicators.note: dis-contented here means emptied of contents, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

explanation.surface: Unhappy lumberjacks look sheepish beside a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' reads as unhappy but means emptied of contents; 'wearing' has those two letters clothed in the sheep's cry.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsa is a tropical American tree whose very light timber is used for models and rafts.

clue.text: Baby bird beginning to eat tip of shoelace

indicators.note: beginning to a word is its opening letter

parts.note: an aglet is the plastic or metal sheath at the end of a lace

explanation.surface: A chick starts nibbling the end of a shoelace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning to' takes E from 'eat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A young eagle still in the nest is called an eaglet, the standard term for its chick.

clue.text: Neutral tone sound recording, possibly a gorilla

indicators.note: sound means the colour word is heard spoken, running on into the next word

parts.note: grey is a neutral colour tone; said aloud before the recording's word, it is heard as the first word of the answer
a tape is a recording

explanation.surface: A flat-toned sound recording might be a gorilla's grunting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' works on GREY, which run together aloud with TAPE is heard as the answer's two words: the T of TAPE does double duty in speech, so the grey part is written GREA.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas, chimps and orangutans are large primates of the hominid family, gorilla being one example.

clue.text: Microphone capturing a gag — absolutely magnificent!

indicators.note: capturing means the first word holds the others inside it

parts.note: mic is the short form of microphone
a gag is a joke, a jest

explanation.surface: A comedian's microphone records a joke that is a triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: Majestic means grand and stately, splendid to an impressive degree, matching something supremely magnificent.

clue.text: Last foxtrot delayed as hot very suddenly

indicators.note: delayed means the letter is put later in the word

parts.note: final means last
Foxtrot is F in the NATO phonetic alphabet
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: The final dance was postponed as the heat suddenly rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delayed' moves F later in FINAL, giving INAFL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in a flash is done in an instant, quick as a lightning bolt.

clue.text: Audition for dangerous part in B movie?

definitions.text: Audition for dangerous part in B movie?

parts.words: Audition for dangerous part in B movie?
parts.note: heard aloud, B is a bee, whose dangerous part is its stinger; the title is also a famous film

explanation.surface: An actor tries out for a risky role in a low-budget film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audition' is not a casting call but hearing: B sounds like 'bee'. A bee's dangerous part is its sting, and the 1973 Newman and Redford con-man caper bears that title.
explanation.definitionFit: A bee can hurt you only with its stinger, and the film of that name is a well-known Hollywood movie.

clue.text: Hard to believe … Hoy broadcast call when riding

parts.note: a tall story is hard to believe

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are spread in a new order

explanation.surface: Amazing: Chris Hoy, the British track cyclist, broadcasting a shout while riding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' shuffles HOY to YHO. Sir Chris Hoy is a British Olympic cycling champion; the riding is fox-hunting on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the cry of a fox-hunting horseman when the quarry is spotted.

clue.text: After changing diapers, I will be off food

indicators.note: after changing, the letters of the word have been rearranged
will be off means that letter departs from the rearranged word

explanation.surface: A parent, having changed a baby's diapers, loses their appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After changing' rearranges DIAPERS and 'will be off' removes the I from them.
explanation.definitionFit: A spread is a lavish meal laid out on the table, or something like butter or paste put on bread.

clue.text: Covered entrance, current century, standing in Iberian city

indicators.note: standing in means placed inside the next word

parts.note: Porto is a city in Portugal
I is the physics symbol for electric current
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: A sheltered doorway in a Portuguese city, with electricity, a hundred years old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing in' puts IC inside PORTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A portico is a porch with a roof held on columns, a sheltered way into a building.

clue.text: Present day worker smiled as he received parcels

indicators.note: parcels says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A modern-day employee grins on receiving deliveries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Present day' looks like 'nowadays' but means Christmas Day, when presents arrive; 'parcels' is the indicator, not the thing received.
explanation.definitionFit: Dasher is one of Santa's reindeer, who toil on Christmas, the day of gifts.

clue.text: Animal consumed food held in both paws

indicators.note: held in means placed inside the letters that follow

parts.note: an animal has right and left paws, R and L
ate means consumed food

explanation.surface: A creature grips its meal in both front paws to eat it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held in' puts ATE inside R and L, the right and left paws.
explanation.definitionFit: The ratel is another name for the honey badger, a fierce African and Asian mammal.

clue.text: Shamelessness of older lady dressed with fine, delicate material

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils

indicators.note: dressed with means wrapped in the clothing that follows

parts.note: lace is a delicate openwork fabric
gran is grandmother, an older lady

explanation.surface: An elderly woman shocks people by wearing fine, flimsy fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed with' puts the older lady inside the fabric, with F for fine before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrance is the quality of being glaringly and brazenly offensive, done openly without embarrassment.

clue.text: Common sense to embrace new words for things

indicators.note: to embrace means the first word holds the letter inside it

parts.note: nous is common sense

explanation.surface: Practical wisdom takes in fresh vocabulary for objects.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, these are naming parts of speech that label people, places and objects.

clue.text: NHS Apr pay reviews — a pain in the backside

indicators.note: an item that is reviewed is looked over again and reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: The April pay review for National Health Service staff is an irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is Britain's National Health Service. The definition is literal: the rash appears on a baby's bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: This skin irritation on a baby's bottom, from wet underwear, is quite literally a sore spot on the rear.

clue.text: With regard to tackling United, become hardened!

indicators.note: tackling here means the first phrase grabs hold of the letter, putting it inside

parts.note: in re is Latin for in the matter of, with regard to
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football team names

explanation.surface: A footballer tackling Manchester United must toughen up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With regard to' is the Latin 'in re' used in legal letters; 'tackling' has it wrap round United's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure is to accustom someone to hardship until they no longer feel it, so they grow tough.

clue.text: Pantomime dame's finale chasing the groom — so funny!

definitions.text: Pantomime dame's finale chasing the groom — so funny!

indicators.note: chasing means coming after the letters that go before it
funny means odd, so the letters are put in a strange order
the phrase's finale is its last letter

explanation.surface: A comic dame in a Christmas pantomime ends the show running after the bridegroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' shuffles THE GROOM SO; E, the finale of 'Pantomime dame', chases them. A pantomime is a British family Christmas stage show where a man plays the comic dame.
explanation.definitionFit: This goose-owning old woman is a classic title role for the comic cross-dressed lead in British Christmas theatre.
